newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat yields seen average to above average.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat yields seen average to above average.

text.p: With the Kansas hard red winter wheat harvest barely underway, agronomists and local agricultural agents said Thursday they were forecasting average to above-average yields across the state.
Talk circulated among traders at the Kansas City Board of Trade that early yields in Sumner County were well above the five-year county average of 27 bushels per acre (bpa).
Traders said they heard talk of yields of 59 to 66 bpa in Sumner County. One trader said he heard a field in South Haven, Kansas, yielded 85 bpa.
"I think those are a little exaggerated," said Ed LeValley, agriculture extension agent for Sumner County, which lies along the Kansas-Oklahoma border.
"There's some good wheat in spots, but there's a lot of double-crop stuff that's thin and full of weeds," LeValley said. "Overall we're probably looking at average to slightly above-average yields."
Under normal conditions, Sumner County is typically the largest wheat-producing county in the state, with a long-term average yield of 32 to 33 bpa, LeValley said.

But production problems during three of the last five years have trimmed the county's five-year average to 27 bushels, according to the Kansas Department of Agricultural Statistics. During the 1995-96 drought, for example, Sumner yielded just 17 bpa.
LeValley also warned against making snap judgments this early in the harvest. He said cutting had just started Wednesday evening in Sumner County and should be well underway this weekend.
David Kehler, agriculture extension agent for Butler County, echoed LeValley's forecast on yields.

"I'd say we're probably a good week away from cutting... I expect that if nothing drastic happens in the next week, it's going to be average to above average," Kehler said of yields in Butler County, which lies northeast of Sumner County.
"I'd say we're going to average 30 to 35 (bpa)," Kehler said. Butler County's five-year average yield is listed at 30.2 bpa. In 1996, it recorded an average yield of 34 bpa.
Kehler said the wheat in his county showed few signs of having been hit by the well-publicized April freeze that sent wheat futures rallying on fears of widespread damage to the U.S. HRW wheat crop.
"I did not find any significant damage after the freeze," Kehler said.
Clear skies through Saturday should allow the hard red winter wheat harvest to begin throughout southern Kansas and advance in Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle, meteorologists said Thursday.
